# Results registry — vocabulary

One noun per concept: **model** (a checkpoint at a pinned revision), **object** (the fitted or declared intervention), **eval** (the benchmark only), **item_set** (its exact prompt set), **instrument** (the declared measurement setting), **run** (one execution), **judgment** / **judge**, **paper_round**, **substrate**. Every controlled value below is a `CHECK` list in the DDL and a validator rule; the evidence column says what produces it.

## `LIFECYCLE_STATES`

| value | evidence |
|---|---|
| `queued` | submit wrapper wrote the planned `run` + `run_state queued` (`sbatch_registered.sh`, Modal launcher). |
| `running` | job start: `run_state running` from the job log / `stage2_common.sh`, with node and job id. |
| `generated` | store writer wrote the completion artifact (`CellStore` results, `bon_served_manifest.json`). |
| `judging` | a judge registered an in-progress `judgment` (the claim; `registry pending-judgment --claim`). |
| `judged` | a `judgment` completed and the judging driver wrote `run_state judged`. |
| `ingested` | harvester `run_ingest` record: completion requirements held (complete judgment with coverage, artifact present). |
| `failed` | scheduler state FAILED/TIMEOUT or a job-log failure line, stored as evidence beside the state. |
| `cancelled` | scheduler state CANCELLED (a STOP sentinel or scancel) with a partial store. |
| `superseded` | a `supersede` ruling covers the run; `superseded_by_run_id` names the successor. |
| `withdrawn` | a source revision no longer carries the run (`withdrawal` record) or a withdrawal ruling. |

| `raw_coefficient` | the all-positions Arditi object: the raw coefficient c on the difference-of-means vector added at every position (battery_curves.parameters.dose_unit; the `arditi_allpos` ladder). Never an alpha: alpha_equiv is a conversion for talking to the prefill-only ladder, not this object's dose. |
| `nominal_only` | a campaign nominal dose (1.0 = the shipped object as served) whose record declares no unit. |
| `unverified` | the record declares no unit (the column default); also the value carried by unsteered and prompted rows, which have no strength. |

## `DECODE_POLICY_MATCH`

| value | evidence |
|---|---|
| `exact` | exactly one decode_policy row admits the run (model, eval or eval category, thinking mode) and every parameter it pins (temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, repetition_penalty, presence_penalty, seed_rule) the run sent at the same value -- or lists under params_not_sent_json and the run did not send -- and the run sent nothing the row leaves null -- or, when several rows in force match and exactly one is eval-scoped, that row over the category-scoped ones (the tie-break of the stamp pass; `extra_json.decode_policy_tiebreak` names the losers); `run.decode_policy_id` names it. Derived by decode_match.stamp_run_rows from v_run_decode_policy_match at the end of every ingest cycle and of a rebuild. Whether the matched row is the FAMILY DEFAULT (the row resolve() returns today for the run's (model, eval-or-category, thinking) key) is a separate fact the paper views render beside it -- `decode_family_default_policy_id` / `decode_is_family_default` in v_paper_current and v_paper_long: `exact` with `decode_is_family_default` 0 reads 'matched a recorded, non-default policy' (every agentic run at the runner's T = 1.0, the vendor preset being every family's default), never a mismatch; the match never reads the default flag. |
| `ambiguous` | several rows match exactly, the effective_from_utc / superseded_by_policy_id windows do not single one out at generated_utc, and neither does the tie-break of the stamp pass (one eval-scoped row over category-scoped rows): a true duplicate policy; the candidates are listed in v_run_decode_policy_match.candidates_json; decode_policy_id stays null. |
| `no_match` | the run recorded sent parameters (decode_sent_json / decode_*_sent) and no row matches them exactly; decode_policy_id is null. |
| `unrecorded` | the run recorded no sent parameter at all (empty decode_sent_json, null decode_*_sent): nothing to verify against. |
| `no_policy` | the producer-written placeholder every run record carries before the derived pass has stamped the row. |

## `SUBSTRATES`

| value | evidence |
|---|---|
| `cluster_a` | a path under cluster A's shared root (the site config) or `SLURM_CLUSTER_NAME`. |
| `cluster_b` | a path under cluster B's shared root (the site config). |
| `modal` | `twosi-fits:` volume or `/vol/` path. |
| `grading_host` | a local path on the registry host; `substrate_source = derived`. Also the registry's spelling of an unknown substrate on `run`: the column admits no `unverified` value, so a run whose substrate no evidence decides carries `substrate = grading_host`, `substrate_source = unverified` and the reason in `field_confidence_json`. |
| `runpod` | standalone pod (`launch.sh` manifest). |
| `slurm` | a Slurm cluster that is neither `cluster_a` nor `cluster_b`: the producer declares it (`SISTEER_REGISTRY_SUBSTRATE=slurm` / `--substrate slurm`) and MUST name the site in `extra_json.cluster_label` (`SISTEER_REGISTRY_CLUSTER_LABEL`); the emitter refuses `slurm` without a label and an unknown substrate by name, never aliasing either to `grading_host`. |

## `CONFIDENCE`

| value | evidence |
|---|---|
| `recorded` | the producer wrote the value. For `substrate`: only a producer field that literally names it (a drive log's `cluster=`, a store's `substrate` field, a manifest's `served_cluster`). |
| `derived` | computed by a documented rule from recorded values. For `substrate`: a routing-table / serving-dir / store path on a shared root, a job-id or cluster-tag prefix -- a prefix is a derivation, never a recorded substrate. |
| `assumed_default` | a documented default filled a value the producer did not write. For `substrate`: what a reader knows about its source as a whole (its submit scripts, its manifests checked once), with the basis in `field_confidence_json`; never filed as `recorded`. |
| `inferred` | a seed value chosen by analogy or read off prose rather than a record (`confidence: inferred` in `configs/registry/*.yaml`, with its `inferred_reason`). |
| `unverified` | unknown; a reason is required in `field_confidence_json`. |

## `DECODE_SEED_RULES`

| value | evidence |
|---|---|
| `per_item` | one seed per item (sha256 of seed_base|trial|readout|item); a seed that closes over more than the item (a turn, a sample) takes the label naming that closure, never `per_item` plus free text. |
| `per_draw` | one seed per best-of-N draw (`bon_seed`). |
| `per_goal_turn` | one seed per (seed_base, goal, turn), seed_base the literal training seed s: the multi-turn target's per-turn rule under the seed-replicate battery (crescendo / pair / actorattack; the attackers keep their own rows). |
| `per_scenario_turn` | one seed per (seed_base, behaviour, scenario_id, turn), seed_base the literal training seed s: the Petri target turns under the seed-replicate battery (the target `GenerateConfig` carries the vendor row + `seed` per scenario-turn; the auditor and the judge are read-outs on their own rows). |
| `per_response` | one seed per (seed_base, family / behaviour, item, sample), seed_base the literal training seed s: the misalignment runner's per-response rule under the seed-replicate battery (`--sampler vendor` + a per-response seed recorded in `meta.json`). |
| `fixed` | one fixed seed for the run. |
| `none` | no seed sent. |
| `unverified` | a superseded instrument whose seeding was never read; reason in `field_confidence_json`. |

## `CHECKPOINT_KINDS`

| value | evidence |
|---|---|
| `base` | a pretrained checkpoint with no chat post-training (the fit checkpoints of the base-to-instruct transfer; never served). |
| `instruct` | an instruction-tuned checkpoint (the served checkpoints of the four families: the -it / -Instruct repos, and Qwen3.5's post-trained checkpoint whose repo name carries no suffix). |
| `chat` | a chat checkpoint with no base / instruct pair (nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-4B-BF16; zai-org/GLM-4.6V-Flash, descoped). |
| `organism` | an emergent-misalignment model organism: a LoRA fine-tune of a served instruct checkpoint on a Betley et al. emergent-misalignment dataset (`scripts/sbatch/em_organism_train.sbatch`), served on its parent as a vLLM LoRA module (`misalign_proxy.sbatch` organisms mode) with the intervention objects overlaid; `extra_json.parent_model_id` names the parent (the schema has no parent column). The organism is the model and `em8q` the eval (organisms are checkpoints, not model + object); `hf_revision` / the adapter sha are `unverified` until the producer sends them. |

## Metric ids

`run_metric.metric_id`, `run_contrast.metric_id` and `eval.headline_metric_id` are free text scoped by the run's eval (`asr`, `over_refusal_graded`, `acc`, `petri_score`, `rate`; the eval is the qualifier, so `acc` on a gsm8k run is a complete name). The naming rule is a BANNED set, rendered as the `*_metric_id_not_generic` CHECK constraints and refused by name in `validate.py` before any insert (`vocab.banned_metric_ids()`):

- A bare generic noun names no statistic: `score`, `value`, `metric`, `result`, `accuracy`, `mean`, `count`, `total`, `number`, `frac`, `fraction`, `share`, `pct`, `percent`, `stat`, `statistic`, `measure`, `outcome`.
- A degeneration statistic belongs in `run_degeneration` (measure × scope, with `measurement_state`) and reaches `run_metric` only through the `frac_*` mirror columns, never as a metric row under an unqualified spelling: `degenerate`, `degeneration`, `degeneracy`, `degen`, `loop`, `looping`, `loops`, `at_cap`, `capped`, `truncated`, `truncation`, `collapse`, `frac_degenerate`, `degenerate_rate`, `degenerate_frac`, `degenerate_fraction`, `loop_rate`, `frac_loop`, `loop_frac`, `at_cap_rate`, `frac_at_cap`, `at_cap_frac`, `at_cap_fraction`, every `DEGENERATION_MEASURES` name as a bare id or as `frac_<measure>` / `<measure>_rate` / `<measure>_frac` / `<measure>_share` / `degen_<measure>_share`, the r2 export's own spellings of the statistics it files as metric rows (`at_cap_share`, `loop_share`, `degenerate_share`, `degenerate_share_union5`, `at_cap_share_retokenized`, `at_cap_share_finish_reason`), and every mirror column name (`frac_at_token_cap`, `frac_degenerate_classifier`, `frac_degenerate_contentless`, `frac_degenerate_rep_ratio_loop`, `frac_degenerate_zlib_collapse`, `frac_degenerate_union5`, `frac_loop_first512`, `frac_defended_degenerate`).
- An eval may accept more than one spelling of its headline: `eval.extra_json.headline_metric_ids` lists them in order of preference (seeded in `configs/registry/evals.yaml`; `strongreject_bon`: `asr`, then `asr_bon_cap4096`, threshold 0.5 both), and a consumer takes the first the run files, else `headline_metric_id` (`paper.headline_metric_ids`; `v_item_headline` applies the same rule in SQL). `headline_metric_id` stays the one declared id (NOT NULL, CHECK-guarded).
- Best-of-N rows are guarded at emission (`vocab.bon_metric_refusal`, called from `emit.RecordWriter.emit_metrics` and `hooks.JudgingScope.metrics`, never from the validator): `asr_bon_cap4096` at a threshold in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75}, `bon_nauc` in {0.5, -1.0} (the AUC's no-threshold sentinel), `asr_at_n<N>` carrying `extra.bon_n` = N; the spelling `asr_at_n_max` is refused for new records and its existing rows stay as legacy (`paper.METRIC_LEGACY` reads them as the `asr` curve point; `producer_metric_spelling` is the provenance).
- A producer's own spelling that differs from the registry id rides `producer_metric_spelling`. The r2 export adapter routes the export's degeneration metric rows (`adapters.r2_export.DEGENERATION_SPELLINGS`) into `run_degeneration` and mirrors the union instrument's readings onto the run's headline `run_metric` row; a qualified statistic no measure names (`residual_at_cap_share_bon_4096`, `at_cap_share_all`, `goal_*_share`, …) stays a metric row.

## Derivation rules (`derive.py`)

- `transfer_kind`: `fit_model_id` vs `run.model_id` — same id → `instruct_direct`; fit on a base checkpoint served on an instruct one → `base_to_instruct`; chat checkpoint → `chat_checkpoint`; system instruction → `prompted_only`; none → `none`.
- `fit_positions`: sidecar precedence `train_budget_meta.json:positions` → `fit_provenance.json:positions_at_fit` → `fit_meta.json:positions` → blob `positions|steer_positions|fit_positions`; Arditi → `searched_post_instruction_span`; diff-mean / CAA / AlphaSteer → `last_token_of_appended_assistant_header`; derived kinds → `inherited_from_parents`.
- `applied_positions_mode`: natively served LoRA → `all`; native residual slot → the standup's served positions; lens → its served-positions key; AlphaSteer → `prefill_last_broadcast`; antidote → `last`; passthrough / none → `none`.
- `multi_turn_steering_scope`: on a multi-turn eval, `all` → `every_turn_prefill_and_decode`, `response` → `final_header_and_current_decode_only`, `response_all_turns` → `every_assistant_span`, prefill-only modes → `prefill_only_each_turn`; single-turn evals → `single_turn`; a `none` object, or a system-instruction object on a multi-turn eval (a prompted object steers no positions, whatever mode the row carries) → `not_applicable`. `history_resent_each_turn = 1` and `decode_scope = per_turn_request` on every current harness.
- `substrate`: a path under cluster A's shared root → cluster_a; under cluster B's → cluster_b (the site configuration names both roots); Modal volume → modal; other local paths → grading_host (`substrate_source = derived`).
- `fit_target_kind`: `derived_meta.json` present → `derived`; a dose stamp (`object.pt.provenance.json:dose_scale` or a `train_budget_meta.json:dose_scaled_from` block) → `derived`, read before the fit record because a dose-scaled copy carries its parent's `train_budget_meta.json`; `none` → `none`; `system_instruction` → `declared_prompt`; `fit_meta.json` or a contrastive kind → `contrastive_direction`; `train_budget_meta.json:si_id` naming a corpus → `corpus_document_fit`, naming a teacher the seeds know (an `si_text` row) with `teacher_forward` → `system_instruction_distillation`; both → refused as ambiguous; nothing → refused, keys listed.
- `decode_resolved_json`: un-sent keys filled from the served snapshot's `generation_config.json` as `not_sent_resolved_to`; a model with no file resolves to the engine defaults marked `assumed_default`.
- degeneration measures: classifier = `eval/degeneracy.py` tail/line loop; contentless = < 10 alphanumerics after unescape; rep-ratio loop = 4-gram repetition > 0.5; zlib collapse = compressed/utf8 < 0.15; union5 = OR of five; at-cap = `finish_reason == length`. `run_metric.frac_*` mirror `run_degeneration`'s `all`-scope rates, never the other way round, and stay NULL when the row's `measurement_state` is not `measured`.
- **`run_degeneration.measurement_state` — a consumer MUST branch on the state, never on a NULL rate.** `measured` rows carry numerator, denominator, denominator_unit and rate; `not_measured` / `not_applicable` / `refused` rows carry NULLs for all four (table CHECK `run_degeneration_measured_pairing`). `v_run_degeneration_wide` exposes `<measure>__<scope>_state` beside every `_rate`.
- structured `ruling.expires_when_json`: a single condition object, or `{kind: any_of|all_of, conditions: [...], guards: [...]}`; `guards` (`input_sha_pinned`, `served_record_at_ruled_point`) are evidence only and can never retire a ruling — a failing guard makes the evaluation `incoherent`; a condition whose evidence is missing / path-absent never counts as held.
- `roster_entry.strength_rule`: `operating_point` | `fixed:<x>` | `ladder:<record_id>` (every strength level the record carries).

## Decode surfaces

Three places state sampling numbers; one is the authority and the other two are derived from or checked against it:

| surface | status |
|---|---|
| `decode_policy` + `sampling_mode_policy` tables, exported to `configs/registry/decode_policy.json` (`registry decode-policy export`, hash-pinned, stamped with the registry `ingest_seq`; `registry decode-policy check`) | the authority; seeded from `configs/registry/decode_policy_seed.yaml` by `registry dimensions load` |
| `sisteer.capeval.tinycap.contracts` sampling tables (`SAMPLING_BY_MODEL_KEY`, `QWEN35_VENDOR_ROWS`, `SERVER_DEFAULT_SAMPLING_BY_MODEL`, `GREEDY_SAMPLING`, `PROTOCOL_SAMPLING_BY_TASK`), best-of-N's per-model vendor preset, the misalignment runner's samplers, the multi-turn target's greedy boundary | derived from the export at import through `sisteer.registry.decode_policy` (stdlib); `tests/test_registry_decode_policy_entry_points.py` pins equality with the oracle fixture under `tests/fixtures/registry/` and that a changed export changes the request bodies |
| `configs/sdfbase_sampled_decode.yaml` (`sisteer.eval.sampled_decode`, the sampled drivers' presets) | a separate statement, agreement-tested against the export-backed table (`tests/test_vendor_sampling_row_agreement.py`) |


## Identity minting (`identity.py`)

Judge and instrument ids are minted by one function each, from canonical fields, by the seeds loader and every adapter alike, so a judgment's `judge_id` and a run's `instrument_id` join the dimension rows whoever wrote them.
- `identity.judge_id(judge_model, rubric_sha256, protocol_sha256, threshold_rule)` = sha256 hex over the canonical JSON (sorted keys) of exactly those four fields; a `judge` row may be passed as one mapping.
- `identity.instrument_id(fields)` = sha256 hex over the canonical JSON of every identity column of the `instrument` table, each normalised to its storage type before hashing (REAL → float so 0 == 0.0; INTEGER → int; JSON columns → the parsed value; None for an absent field): `eval_id` (TEXT), `item_set_id` (TEXT), `harness` (TEXT), `harness_version` (TEXT), `harness_config_hash` (TEXT), `n_shot` (INTEGER), `prompt_template_sha256` (TEXT), `cot_prompting` (TEXT), `scoring_rule` (TEXT), `answer_extraction` (TEXT), `token_cap_tokens` (INTEGER), `token_cap_ladder_json` (JSON), `ladder_promotion_rule` (TEXT), `read_at` (TEXT), `reply_cap_tokens` (INTEGER), `context_window_tokens` (INTEGER), `decode_source` (TEXT), `decode_temperature` (REAL), `decode_top_p` (REAL), `decode_top_k` (INTEGER), `decode_min_p` (REAL), `decode_repetition_penalty` (REAL), `decode_presence_penalty` (REAL), `decode_seed_rule` (TEXT), `thinking_mode` (TEXT), `n_trials` (INTEGER), `bon_n` (INTEGER), `max_turns` (INTEGER), `serving_path` (TEXT), `applied_positions_mode` (TEXT), `attacker_model_id` (TEXT), `attacker_decode_json` (JSON), `judge_id` (TEXT), `prefill_scheme` (TEXT), `padding_tokens` (INTEGER), `padding_identity_sha256` (TEXT). The alias spellings `temperature`→`decode_temperature`, `top_p`→`decode_top_p`, `top_k`→`decode_top_k`, `min_p`→`decode_min_p`, `repetition_penalty`→`decode_repetition_penalty`, `presence_penalty`→`decode_presence_penalty`, `token_cap_ladder`→`token_cap_ladder_json` fold onto the column names, so an `instrument` row, a seed row and a policy row mint one id. Only `notes`, `extra_json`, `field_confidence_json` and the harvester tail are outside the identity. `padding_identity_sha256`, `padding_tokens` are omitted from the canonical JSON while NULL (`identity.INSTRUMENT_ID_OPTIONAL_FIELDS`): an unpadded instrument hashes as it did before the padding fields existed, and a padded one is another instrument (`padding_identity_sha256` = `identity.padding_identity_sha256(block)`, sha256 over the canonical JSON of the filler contract `filler_sha256`, `mode`, `placement`, `separator`, `tolerance`).

## Legacy-term mapping

Older words of the producing harnesses map to registry nouns as follows. This block is the one place they are spelled outside `_legacy` columns (the vocabulary test exempts it).

|---|---|---|
| arm | object (`object_id`, `paper_label`, `object_role`) | `campaign_cell_id_legacy`, `producer_object_key_legacy` |
| cell | run (one execution) or object, by context | `campaign_cell_id_legacy` |
| lane | source of a paper row / transfer setting | `lane_source_legacy`, `transfer_kind` |
| view | model_id + transfer_kind | `view_legacy` |
| leg | run | `producer_run_key_legacy` |
| wave | campaign | `campaign` |
| grader | judge / judgment | `judge_id`, `judgment_id` |
| psr | relu_steer | `producer_spellings_json`, `campaign_cell_id_legacy` |
| rung (dose sense) | strength_nominal | `operating_point_id_legacy` |
| rung (cap sense) | token_cap_rung_index | — |
| dose | strength_nominal / strength_coefficient | — |
| pass (bare) | pass_label | — |
| cluster (bare) | substrate | — |
| r2 (bare) | paper_round | — |
| component | eval_category | — |
| family (of models) | model.family | — |
